_comment: Canonical machine-readable index of Carlos Duarte's backtested trading strategies. This file is the single source of truth for (a) the Trading_Index AI hub and (b) the LTCMA website Backtests page (docs/backtests.html, generated by ~/LTCMA/scripts/24_backtests.py). To register a new strategy: append an object to 'strategies' and re-run that script (or the LTCMA daily refresh). Verdict/metric values are pulled verbatim from each backtest's REPORT.md; where a metric was not computed in that report it is the string 'n/a' (never guess). badge: green=Deployable (clears <10% DD survival bar AND beats S&P), yellow=Ensemble component (real edge, not standalone-worthy), red=Pass/no edge (failed cost-adjusted tests).
protocol: Optuna smart-search -> walk-forward + purged CV -> Deflated Sharpe (DSR) + PBO -> Monte Carlo 100k-500k -> post-2024 held-out -> S&P 500 gate -> survival bar (max DD < 10%). Cost model: pessimistic retail (FxPro embedded per-bar spread + markup + stop slippage). Sizing: 1% fixed-fractional (R-multiple, sizing-invariant Sharpe).

strategies.name: Candle Range Theory (CRT)
strategies.what_it_tests: ICT 3-candle range theory: candle 1 sets a range, candle 2 sweeps a side and closes back inside (liquidity grab), candle 3 enters the opposite way. Tested vanilla and with regime overlays (200-EMA trend alignment, ATR regime, day-of-week) on EURUSD, USDJPY, Gold and Silver.
strategies.verdict_line: Vanilla CRT has no post-cost edge (only 3 of 448 variations cleared IS+OOS). CRT plus a daily-200EMA trend filter on Gold is a real but thin edge (Calmar 0.33) - usable only as one signal inside the regime-adaptive ensemble, never standalone.

key_metrics.headline_config: GOLD daily HTF, 3R target, + daily 200-EMA trend filter (507 trades, win 37%)

strategies.metrics_note: This report predates the full standing protocol: it used walk-forward IS (2016-2022) / OOS (2023-2026) but did NOT compute Deflated Sharpe or PBO, hence DSR/PBO = n/a.

strategies.name: Breedon & Ranaldo Local-Hours FX Rotation
strategies.what_it_tests: Published intraday FX pattern (SNB WP 2011-04): a currency tends to depreciate during its own country's trading hours and appreciate during foreign hours. Short/long each currency during its local session across EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, EURJPY, GBPJPY.
strategies.verdict_line: NOT DEPLOYABLE on any of the 5 pairs. The structural effect is real but tiny (EUR depreciates in Frankfurt morning) and smaller than realistic retail round-trip cost; every positive in-sample config fails DSR, held-out 2025+, Monte Carlo and the S&P gate. The intraday pattern appears largely decayed since its 2000s sample.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD EUR-short, Frankfurt 10:00, 4h hold, ATR x2.5, news-skip (best of 5 pairs; still fails)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the EURUSD leg (the only pair with positive full-period Sharpe); the other four are negative even in-sample. DSR 0.000 because raw SR 0.45 << noise-expected SR0 2.29 over 3000 trials. Held-out 2025+ Sharpe -0.45 (reverses). S&P bar: CAGR 11.91%, Sharpe 0.74, maxDD -33.92%.

strategies.name: Buy-the-Dip / Sell-the-Rip
strategies.what_it_tests: Daily-timeframe pullback-in-uptrend (systemic alpha): buy dips while price is above a long trend filter, optionally short rips in downtrends. Universe: SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM/EFA/EEM/EWW/GLD/SLV ETFs plus Gold/Silver spot, 2010-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: Robust but boring: 80-99% of the parameter space is positive-Calmar, so the edge is structural, not curve-fit. Deploy as a diversified SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble, not a single name. It is a drawdown-reducer / S&P-replacement-at-lower-risk, NOT a return amplifier: at a 10% DD budget the ensemble earns ~10.1% CAGR vs a de-levered S&P's ~3.6%. 'Sell the rip' added nothing (10/11 configs went long-only).

key_metrics.headline_config: SPY flagship (DSR 0.80); robust survivors that beat S&P Calmar: EFA, QQQ, SPY. maxDD/CAGR shown @1% risk.

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the SPY selected config (highest DSR alongside QQQ). maxDD -4.3% and CAGR 2.9% are at 1% fixed-fractional risk (in cash most days); scaled to a 10% DD budget the SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble earns ~10.1% CAGR. PBO range across instruments 0.37 (QQQ) to 0.85 (EWW). S&P full-window: CAGR 12.2%, maxDD -33.9%, Calmar 0.36.

strategies.name: Momentum Rotation TAA
strategies.what_it_tests: Antonacci/Faber-style tactical asset allocation: rank a pool of ETFs by trailing momentum, hold the top-N, with an absolute-momentum (trend) crash filter. Monthly/weekly/quarterly rebalance, 2011-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: PASS on rotation as standalone alpha. The only thing that survives deflation is plain diversification - a static equal-weight SPY/IEF/GLD sleeve (Sharpe 1.00, DSR 0.96) - which is NOT rotation. Relative momentum only helps in a broad pool with chronic laggards to avoid; in a tight good-diversifier pool it hurts. Nothing clears the <10% DD survival bar, and the best rotation's headline is a month-end timing artifact (jitter blows DD to -36%).

key_metrics.headline_config: Pool A: 6m lookback, top-3/8, monthly, abs-mom filter (best genuine rotation; still fails survival bar + fragile)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are Pool A (best genuine rotation). DSR 0.91 is high only because the 216 grid configs are near-clones (mild deflation) - it means 'real positive-Sharpe portfolio', NOT 'rotation beats buy-and-hold'. PBO 0.30 full grid / 0.35 rotation subset. The deployable byproduct is the static SPY/IEF/GLD sleeve (Sharpe 1.00, DSR 0.96, maxDD -16.9%); keep the abs-momentum filter as a crash overlay. SPY buy&hold CAGR 14.2% (untouchable on raw return).
